headline: Google's illegal Finland forest clearing for datacentre draws order to halt, wolves
summary: Google was ordered to stop work at two Finnish sites after illegally felling a large area of forest for a datacentre near Muhos. Outlets give different figures for the area cleared, and report that wolves which used to live in the forest are now roaming into nearby villages.

claims.statement: Google was ordered to stop work at two Finnish sites after illegally felling an estimated 250,000 trees for a datacentre.

sources.quote: ‘Pure arrogance’: anger in Finland as Google illegally fells 250,000 trees for datacentre

claims.statement: The Guardian said the cleared area covered 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest near the town of Muhos.

sources.quote: the 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest near the town of Muhos

claims.statement: Tom's Hardware said Google destroyed 1,300 acres of forest in Finland for AI data centers.

sources.quote: Wolves roam into Finnish villages after Google destroys 1,300 acres of forest for AI data centers

claims.statement: Wolves that used to live in the cleared forests are now roaming into nearby Finnish villages.

sources.quote: Wolves, who used to live in the forests recently cleared for Google data center development, are now roaming into Finnish villages nearby.

discrepancies.explanation: The Guardian gives the cleared forest area as 330 hectares (815 acres), while Tom's Hardware puts it at 1,300 acres for the same Google datacentre clearing.

quotes.quote: 1,300 acres of forest for AI data centers
